statement: construct_array n k returns a result r, and the following hold: (a) len(r) = n; (b) for every i with 0 <= i < len(r), 1 <= r[i] <= n; (c) for all i, j with 0 <= i < j < len(r), r[i] != r[j]; (d) for D = { |r[i] - r[i+1]| : 0 <= i < len(r)-1 }, the cardinality |D| is exactly k. Consequently r is a permutation of the integers 1,2,...,n and the adjacent absolute differences have exactly k distinct values.
preconditions: n and k are Std.I64 values satisfying 1 <= k < n <= 10000.

statement: For every such n and k, construct_array n k returns a result r; it does not fail, panic, overflow, or access an out-of-bounds index.
preconditions: n and k are Std.I64 values satisfying 1 <= k < n <= 10000.

statement: Whenever construct_array n k returns a result r, len(r) = n.
preconditions: n and k are Std.I64 values satisfying 1 <= k < n <= 10000.

statement: Whenever construct_array n k returns a result r, for every index i with 0 <= i < len(r), we have 1 <= r[i] <= n.
preconditions: n and k are Std.I64 values satisfying 1 <= k < n <= 10000.

statement: Whenever construct_array n k returns a result r, for all indices i and j with 0 <= i < j < len(r), r[i] != r[j].
preconditions: n and k are Std.I64 values satisfying 1 <= k < n <= 10000.

statement: Whenever construct_array n k returns a result r, for every value v with 1 <= v <= n there exists exactly one index i with 0 <= i < len(r) such that r[i] = v.
preconditions: n and k are Std.I64 values satisfying 1 <= k < n <= 10000.

statement: Whenever construct_array n k returns a result r, for every i with 0 <= i < len(r)-1, |r[i] - r[i+1]| > 0.
preconditions: n and k are Std.I64 values satisfying 1 <= k < n <= 10000.

statement: Whenever construct_array n k returns a result r, for every i with 0 <= i < len(r)-1, |r[i] - r[i+1]| <= n-1.
preconditions: n and k are Std.I64 values satisfying 1 <= k < n <= 10000.

statement: Whenever construct_array n k returns a result r, there exists a finite set T of positive integers such that |T| <= k and for every i with 0 <= i < len(r)-1, |r[i] - r[i+1]| is an element of T.
preconditions: n and k are Std.I64 values satisfying 1 <= k < n <= 10000.

statement: Whenever construct_array n k returns a result r, let D = { |r[i] - r[i+1]| : 0 <= i < len(r)-1 }. Then |D| >= k.
preconditions: n and k are Std.I64 values satisfying 1 <= k < n <= 10000.

statement: Whenever construct_array n k returns a result r, the sum of all entries of r, interpreted as mathematical integers, satisfies sum_{i=0}^{len(r)-1} r[i] = n*(n+1)/2.
preconditions: n and k are Std.I64 values satisfying 1 <= k < n <= 10000.

statement: Whenever construct_array n k returns a result r, the minimum entry of r is 1 and the maximum entry of r is n.
preconditions: n and k are Std.I64 values satisfying 1 <= k < n <= 10000.
